headline: SEBON Chair Bhatt vows to resolve market problems, Says he may seek ordinance if new securities act delayed
body: KATHMANDU: Securities Board of Nepal (SEBON) Chairman Dr. Gopal Bhatt has said he is prepared to take even an ordinance route to address longstanding legal and regulatory problems in Nepal’s capital market if the proposed new Securities Act continues to face delays. Bhatt made the remarks during a meeting with a delegation from the Nepal Share Market Investors Association, where he pledged to take concrete measures to improve the stock market, strengthen transparency and protect the interests of retail investors. According to participants, Bhatt said that if the process of drafting and endorsing a new securities law takes longer than expected, he would be ready to pursue an ordinance-based solution to address issues that cannot be resolved under the existing legal framework. The statement comes at a time when investors have been increasingly demanding stronger regulatory action against market manipulation, insider trading and the spread of misleading information through social media. Investor protection is priority, says SEBON chief During the meeting, Chairman Bhatt said investor protection and market transparency would remain among his primary responsibilities. He said the board had already started working on market reforms and urged investors to make investment decisions based on the fundamental and actual condition of companies and the market rather than rumors. Bhatt also said SEBON would intensify investor-awareness programs to help retail investors better understand market risks and make informed investment decisions. The delegation led by association Vice-President Bhagwan Bahadur Rawat included General Secretary Rabin Kandel and executive committee members Rishi Bhetwal and Vivek Shrestha. Investors question weak action against market manipulation The investors’ representatives raised concerns over several persistent problems in Nepal’s capital market. They questioned the regulator’s response to allegations of insider trading, artificial price manipulation and misleading rumors circulated through social media platforms. The delegation argued that market volatility driven by rumors and speculation can put the savings of small and retail investors at significant risk. The representatives also criticized what they described as a longstanding pattern in which regulatory authorities issue assurances but major market-related cases are investigated for years, while penalties imposed in serious cases remain relatively weak. The investors warned that merely issuing statements and imposing nominal fines would not be sufficient to restore confidence in the capital market. Economic slowdown and idle liquidity also discussed The investors’ delegation also highlighted broader economic concerns. Vice-President Rawat pointed to Nepal’s economic growth rate falling below 3 percent and expressed concern that, despite sufficient liquidity in the banking system, credit has not been flowing adequately into productive sectors. He argued that Nepal’s stock market should not become a mechanism through which only a limited group of investors makes profits. Instead, he said, the capital market should function as an effective mechanism for mobilizing savings and channeling capital toward productive economic activities. The delegation stressed that strengthening the stock market would require improvements in transparency, corporate governance, enforcement and investor confidence. Bhatt promises progress on short selling and intraday trading One of the key issues discussed during the meeting was the introduction of short selling and intraday trading in Nepal’s stock market. Chairman Bhatt said he had studied, taught and advocated issues related to short selling and intraday trading for a long period and claimed that preparations were now underway to introduce them in practical terms. He said the necessary work was being accelerated and assured the investors that they would be able to use these facilities in the near future. The introduction of short selling and intraday trading has long been discussed as part of the modernization of Nepal’s capital market. Short selling can allow investors to take positions based on expectations of falling prices, while intraday trading enables investors to buy and sell securities within the same trading session. However, both mechanisms require robust risk-management systems, surveillance infrastructure and clear regulatory safeguards. SEBON plans infrastructure and structural upgrades Bhatt also pledged to strengthen SEBON’s internal infrastructure and institutional capacity as part of the broader modernization of the securities market. According to him, regulatory capacity must evolve alongside the market and technological changes taking place in the financial sector. The investors’ delegation, however, urged the board to translate its commitments into measurable action. General Secretary Rabin Kandel said the regulator should move beyond assurances and public announcements and instead adopt a stronger approach to regulation and enforcement. He said the white paper recently presented by the new SEBON leadership was a positive development, but its implementation should be accompanied by clear deadlines and measurable targets. Investors warn of declining confidence The association warned that continued failure to protect the savings of ordinary investors could seriously undermine confidence in Nepal’s capital market. According to the delegation, if investors do not see meaningful action on issues affecting them, it would become increasingly difficult to have full confidence in the activities of the securities regulator. The investors also argued that declining confidence in the capital market could have broader implications for governance and institutional credibility. They called on SEBON to demonstrate through concrete action that investor protection, transparency and market integrity are not merely policy commitments. Ordinance remark puts focus on legal reform Bhatt’s statement regarding the possibility of resolving outstanding issues through an ordinance has placed renewed attention on the delay in replacing Nepal’s existing securities legislation. A modern securities law is considered necessary to provide regulators with stronger tools to respond to new forms of market manipulation, technological developments and evolving trading practices. The proposed legal framework is also expected to clarify the regulatory powers required to strengthen enforcement and modernize market operations. For investors, however, the immediate concern is whether regulatory reforms will translate into stronger enforcement and greater protection of retail investors. With the new SEBON leadership promising action on market modernization, short selling, intraday trading, investor awareness and institutional capacity, the coming months are likely to be closely watched by market participants. The key test for the regulator will now be whether these commitments can be converted into specific regulatory actions, clear timelines and effective enforcement—rather than remaining limited to assurances. Bhatt’s willingness to consider an ordinance if legislative delays continue signals an attempt to accelerate the reform process, but the effectiveness of the proposed changes will ultimately depend on implementation and the regulator’s ability to enforce market rules consistently. headline: Nepal Stock Market falls 19 points as NEPSE slips to 2,622 points
body: KATHMANDU: Nepal’s stock market extended its decline on Tuesday, with the Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) index falling 19.34 points as selling pressure intensified across most sectors. Following Tuesday’s trading session, the NEPSE index stood at 2,622 points. The decline was significantly larger than Monday’s 2.25-point drop, indicating increased selling pressure in the market. Of the companies traded on Tuesday, 57 recorded gains, while 217 declined and five remained unchanged. Trading turnover also declines Market turnover also decreased compared to the previous trading session. Total turnover stood at around Rs 5.07 billion on Tuesday, down from Rs 5.52 billion recorded on Monday. The decline came despite continued significant trading activity in the hydropower sector, which accounted for the largest share of total market turnover. Most sectors decline All sectoral indices except the trading group declined on Tuesday. The Trading sector gained 0.41%, while the Manufacturing and Processing sector recorded the steepest decline, falling 1.40%. Other sectoral indices also closed lower: Banking: -0.59% Development Bank: -0.59% Finance: -0.41% Hotels and Tourism: -0.84% Hydropower: -0.92% Investment: -0.83% Life Insurance: -0.76% Microfinance: -0.39% Non-Life Insurance: -0.57% Others: -0.97% The broad-based decline indicates that selling pressure was not confined to a single segment of the market. Hydropower stocks dominate turnover Hydropower companies remained the most actively traded segment, with the sector recording turnover of approximately Rs 2.53 billion. Commercial banks recorded turnover of around Rs 440 million, while companies in the manufacturing and processing sector generated transactions worth approximately Rs 450 million. Among individual companies, Solu Hydropower, Khanikhola Hydropower, Reliance Spinning Mills, United Modi Hydropower and Ridi Power were among the most heavily traded stocks by transaction value. Top gainers and losers Recently listed companies Sarvottam Paints and Mount Everest Power gained around 15% each, emerging among the day’s strongest performers. Similarly, Manakamana Engineering Hydropower gained 4.78%, while Upper Mailung Khola Hydropower rose 3.64%. On the declining side, Sagarmatha Jalabidyut Company fell 10.63%, while Khanikhola Hydropower dropped 9.40%. Saptakoshi Development Bank declined 6.65%. The sharp fall in the NEPSE index, coupled with declines across most sectoral indices, reflects a weaker market sentiment on Tuesday. Investors are now closely watching whether the selling pressure will continue in the coming sessions or whether the market will find support around the current level. headline: Brokerages Earn Over Rs 41.27 Crore in Commission in Shrawan; Nasa Securities Tops List
body: KATHMANDU: Nepal’s stockbroking companies earned more than Rs 41 crore in commission income during the first month of the current fiscal year, with Nasa Securities emerging as the highest-earning brokerage in Shrawan. According to data published by the Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE), 91 securities brokerage companies collectively generated Rs 41.27 crore in commission income in Shrawan. The total commission income increased by 7.16 percent, or approximately Rs 2.76 crore, compared with the previous month. Brokerage companies had earned Rs 38.51 crore in commission in Ashadh. Nasa Securities Tops Broker Commission Earnings Nasa Securities Company Limited, broker number 58, recorded the highest commission income during Shrawan. The company earned Rs 3.82 crore in commission during the month. Sani Securities Company (broker no. 42) ranked second with Rs 1.40 crore, followed by Imperial Securities Company (broker no. 45), which earned Rs 1.32 crore. Vision Securities (broker no. 34) generated Rs 1.32 crore, while Online Securities (broker no. 49) earned Rs 1.31 crore in commission. Other major brokerage companies among the top earners included Trishakti Securities (broker no. 48), with Rs 1.21 crore, and Dipshikha Dhitopatra Karobar Company (broker no. 38), with Rs 1.03 crore. Dynamic Money Managers Securities (broker no. 44) earned around Rs 1.02 crore, while Aryatara Investment & Securities (broker no. 57) generated approximately Rs 1 crore in commission. ABC Securities (broker no. 17) earned Rs 86.75 lakh during the month. Other Major Brokerages Kohinoor Investment & Securities (broker no. 35) earned Rs 85.08 lakh, while Capital Max Securities (broker no. 62) generated Rs 83.79 lakh. Nabil Stock Dealer (broker no. 77) earned Rs 82.41 lakh, Premier Securities (broker no. 32) earned Rs 77.61 lakh, and Nepal Stock House (broker no. 14) generated Rs 75.12 lakh. Similarly, Sumeru Securities (broker no. 39) earned Rs 70.90 lakh, Lynch Stock Market (broker no. 41) generated Rs 70.60 lakh, and Shri Hari Securities (broker no. 56) earned Rs 67.57 lakh. Kalash Stock Market (broker no. 74) generated Rs 63.65 lakh, while Nagarik Stock Dealer (broker no. 60) earned Rs 60.53 lakh in commission. Money World Earns the Lowest Commission At the other end of the list, Money World Share Exchange (broker no. 73) recorded the lowest commission income among the brokerages listed in the NEPSE data. The company earned just Rs 705 in commission during Shrawan. Pahi Investment (broker no. 79) earned Rs 62,309, while Garima Securities (broker no. 78) generated Rs 4.09 lakh. TradeMo Securities (broker no. 98) earned Rs 5 lakh, Beni Securities (broker no. 93) generated Rs 5.81 lakh, and Sajilo Broker (broker no. 90) earned Rs 6.88 lakh. Elite Stock House (broker no. 68) earned Rs 12,902, while Sagarmatha Securities (broker no. 18) generated Rs 10.96 lakh. Swarnalakshmi Securities (broker no. 37) earned Rs 10.84 lakh, Bhole Ganesh Securities (broker no. 61) earned Rs 10,782, and RBB Securities (broker no. 97) generated Rs 8.71 lakh. The rise in brokerage commission income in Shrawan compared with Ashadh reflects increased securities trading activity and higher transaction-based earnings for brokerage companies during the month.
